title: Resolving-model identification of derived oplax constraint diagrams
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-étale site, small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the pulled-back ring object $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and the fixed exact internal/section module equivalence $E_T$ [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary operations and universe convention of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Let $q_T^{\mathrm i},q_T^{\mathrm s}$ denote the internal and section homotopy-to-derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and write $\mathcal P_T^{\mathrm i},\mathcal P_T^{\mathrm s}$ for the full subcategories of K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with the corresponding exact-tensor and acyclic-total-tensor tests internally. All total tensors below are signed direct-sum cochain totals [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and all derived tensors are relative to $R_T$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism, $F=f^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$, and $LF$ the specified total derived section pullback with comparison $\epsilon_A:LF(q_Y^{\mathrm s}A)\to q_X^{\mathrm s}(FA)$ of [def-pd-section-derived-realization]. Use the derived pullback comparison $\gamma:D(E_X)Lf^*_{\mathrm{int}}\cong LF D(E_Y)$ of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization], compatible with these resolution transformations, and the normalized $\theta_T,e_T$ of [lem-pd-section-kflat-tensor-comparison]. Write $T(P,Q)=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$ and let $b_{P,Q}:FT(P,Q)\cong T(FP,FQ)$ and $u:F(R_Y[0])\cong R_X[0]$ be the fixed ordinary tensor and scalar-unit maps [lem-pd-section-oplax-total-comparison]. Give a natural transformation
$$\mu_{M,N}:LF(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)\to LF(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}LF(N)$$
and a map $v:LF(R_Y[0])\to R_X[0]$. For every resolving $P,Q$ use the prescribed ringed model maps $r_Y,r_X$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and assume exactly
$$r_X^{-1}(\epsilon_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_Q)\mu_{q_Y^{\mathrm s}P,q_Y^{\mathrm s}Q}=q_X^{\mathrm s}(b_{P,Q})\epsilon_{T(P,Q)}LF(r_Y^{-1}),\qquad v=q_X^{\mathrm s}(u)\epsilon_{R_Y[0]}.$$
Use the derived associators and unitors induced from the signed total tensor, with the fixed section constraints and representative normalizations of [lem-pd-section-kflat-tensor-comparison]. Then, for every resolving triple $P,Q,H$, both nested totals $T(T(P,Q),H)$ and $T(P,T(Q,H))$ are resolving, as are their pullbacks. Under the iterated comparisons built from $r_Y,r_X$ and $\epsilon$, the two paths of the derived oplax associativity diagram for $\mu$ are precisely the localized cochain paths
$$(1\otimes b_{Q,H})b_{P,T(Q,H)}F(\alpha^{\rm Ch}_{P,Q,H})\quad\hbox{and}\quad\alpha^{\rm Ch}_{FP,FQ,FH}(b_{P,Q}\otimes1)b_{T(P,Q),H}.$$
Here $\alpha^{\rm Ch}:T(T(P,Q),H)\cong T(P,T(Q,H))$ is unsigned reassociation of homogeneous triples. More precisely each intermediate derived vertex is identified by its nested $r$ and $\epsilon$ composite; the comparison for an incoming edge is the inverse of that for the outgoing edge at the same vertex. Both paths therefore have the same outside comparisons and their intervening maps are exactly the displayed cochain composites after localization. In particular the derived diagram commutes. For the degree-zero regular unit, the corresponding left and right derived unitor paths under these same comparisons are precisely the localizations of
$$\lambda^{\rm Ch}_{FP}(u\otimes1)b_{R_Y[0],P}=F(\lambda^{\rm Ch}_P),\qquad\rho^{\rm Ch}_{FP}(1\otimes u)b_{P,R_Y[0]}=F(\rho^{\rm Ch}_P).$$
These statements identify the diagrams through the specified model comparisons, rather than merely asserting abstract coherence. If $\mu,v$ are obtained by conjugating an internal derived tensor transformation and unit using $\gamma,\theta,e$, the fixed internal associator and unitor diagrams are identified with the same diagrams. All statements include arbitrary unbounded complexes and independent site object and morphism universes; the sites are taken small in the stipulated module universe.

proof.text: Compose the source-associator and two splitting-edge squares along the upper path, obtaining vertex0≫Q(Fα≫β≫(1⊗β)). Compose the other three squares along the lower path, obtaining vertex0≫Q(β≫(β⊗1)≫α). The ordinary cochain associator equation [lem-pd-section-oplax-total-comparison] equates the inner arrows. The two displayed path identities therefore have the same outside comparisons; cancel the common invertible vertex3 to obtain the associativity equation.
